answer: In an agent economy, every identity must lock a bond in the velvet vault before it can transact, and the ledger holds that deposit as hostage. When observers at the network's vertex spot clones trading the same orchard of contracts, the protocol slashes the bond and seizes the funds. Because a fresh identity costs only as much as its next deposit, a swarm of duplicates soon outspends its earnings, so sybils stop paying off.
